title: PGL linearizations, invariant section algebras, and geometric stability
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\geq1$, $Z$ a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme], and $L$ an $\mathcal O_Z$-module. A PGL-linearization of $L$ consists of a natural left action of $\mathrm{GL}_r(T)=\mathrm{GL}_r(\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T))$ on $\operatorname{Mor}_k(T,Z)$ for every test scheme $T/k$, and $\mathcal O_T$-linear isomorphisms $x^*L\simeq(gx)^*L$, natural under every test morphism, satisfying the identity and multiplication cocycles. Scalar matrices act identically on both the scheme and module. Equivalently this is an action and linearization of the fppf quotient group sheaf $\mathrm{PGL}_{r,k}=\mathrm{GL}_{r,k}/\mathbf G_m$; no global lifting of PGL-valued test points is required. For an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], use the canonical monoidal tensor-power pullback identifications to define invariant sections of $L^{\otimes n}$ by equality of their pullbacks after these isomorphisms on every test scheme, including nonreduced schemes. A geometric point is semistable if some invariant section of positive degree pulls back nontrivially, and stable if in addition its orbit is closed in the semistable locus after base change to its algebraically closed field of values and its PGL stabilizer has dimension zero. Equivalently, on an algebraically closed field the latter stabilizer has finitely many PGL classes of matrices; this allows nonreduced finite stabilizers. Inside the section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], the invariant ring is the subring generated by its homogeneous invariant sections, with degree subgroups inherited from the section ring; these subgroups admit a unique graded-ring decomposition. The constants are the structure pullbacks in degree zero. Finite generation over $k$ means generation as a ring by these constants and finitely many elements. A degree-$d$ Veronese is generated in degree one over degree zero if every degree-$nd$ element belongs to the subring generated by degrees zero and $d$. Its invariant Proj [def-pc-proj] is taken with the structure map induced by a degree-zero coefficient homomorphism agreeing with these constants. Restriction to a subscheme requires equivariance of both the action and the pullback line isomorphisms. An invariant subscheme is invariant on all scheme-valued test points; an invariant map to an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] identifies all such translates. Morphisms to algebraic spaces are natural transformations from the represented functor. All scheme and coefficient objects and all test schemes use one fixed universe $u$, with their categories in $u+1$.

proof.text: For invariantGrading_existsUnique, inherit one_mem and mul_mem on invariantGrade from sectionRingGrade through the subring inclusion. Map each inherited degree subgroup additively to its ambient section-ring degree subgroup by forgetting invariant-ring membership. DirectSum.map of these maps is injective by componentwise subtype injectivity. Its composite with ambient recomposition is invariant-ring recomposition followed by the subring inclusion; verify this identity on each summand. Ambient recomposition is injective by sectionRing_isInternal, so inherited recomposition is injective.

Use the inherited graded multiplication to make recomposition a ring homomorphism from the direct sum of invariantGrade into invariantRing, and compose with the ambient inclusion. The range subring of this composite contains each generating homogeneous invariant section: insert that section as a single summand in its degree, with invariant-ring membership supplied by Subring.subset_closure. Subring.closure_le therefore places the entire invariantRing inside this range. Subtype extensionality then gives surjectivity of inherited recomposition.

The bijective recomposition gives IsInternal invariantGrade. Its chooseDecomposition, together with the inherited graded multiplication, supplies GradedRing invariantGrade. Any two such structures agree: the graded multiplication laws are propositions and DirectSum.Decomposition is subsingleton. This proves existence and uniqueness without any separate closure lemma for invariant tensor products.
